  - **Communication Driver**: **Modbus/TCP** [Source 1].
- Set the connected device’s **IP address**, **timeout**, **communication start wait time**, and **Communication Error Indication** option [Source 1].
per_question.expected_answer: The NA connects via Modbus/TCP (Communication Driver "Modbus/TCP", Device Series "CK3"), and the command Sys.ModbusServerEnable=1 must be entered from the PowerPMAC IDE terminal.

per_question.expected_answer: The HMIGTO1300, HMIGTO1310 and HMIGTO2300 have no SD card interface; all other GTO models (HMIGTO2310, 3510, 4310, 5310, 6310 and the 2315/5315/6315 stainless versions) accept the 4 GB SD card HMIZSD4G.

per_question.question: How do you replace the real-time clock battery in an Allen-Bradley PanelView Plus 7 Standard terminal (e.g. 2711P-T10C21D8S)?
per_question.answer:
The provided Standard technical data tables cover 4/6-in and 12/15-in terminals and do not explicitly list **2711P-T10C21D8S** [Source 1, 8].  

For PanelView Plus 7 Standard terminals, the real-time clock backup battery replacement is a **CR2032 lithium coin cell** [Source 1, 8], with Allen-Bradley part number **2711P-RY2032** [Source 1].  

A related PanelView Plus 7 Performance manual describes battery access as: remove power, loosen the screws securing the logic module to the back of the display, then lift the logic module away from the display module and turn it over to expose the circuit board [Source 6].  

Replace only with catalog number **2711P-RY2032** or an equivalent **CR2032** coin-cell, and do not replace the battery unless power has been removed and the area is known to be nonhazardous [Source 6].
per_question.expected_answer: 1) Disconnect power from the terminal. 2) Remove the battery cover by rotating it from C (closed) to O (open). 3) Press the vertical center tab on the metal latch away from the battery to release it. 4) Insert the new battery (2711P-RY2032 / CR2032) at an angle under the metal latch with the + side up. 5) Gently press down on the opposite side until it locks into place. 6) Replace the cover and rotate it from O (open) to C (closed).

per_question.question: What are the steps to mount an Allen-Bradley PanelView 5510 stainless-steel terminal (e.g. 2715P-T12WD-BSK) in a panel, and what torque is applied to the mounting clips?
per_question.answer:
For the **PanelView 5510 stainless-steel terminal 2715P-T12WD-BSK**, use **2711P-RTMC mounting clips** [Source 1, 5]. The **2715P-T12WD-BSK** is listed as a PanelView 5510 Stainless Steel Terminal catalog number [Source 4].

### Mounting clips required
- **2715P-T12WD-BSK requires 10 mounting clips** [Source 5].
- Each **2711P-RTMC** mounting clip kit contains **8 clips** [Source 5].
- If more than 8 clips are needed, order **two 2711P-RTMC mounting clip kits** [Source 5].
- Mounting clips secure the stainless-steel terminal in a panel, and the number of clips varies by terminal size [Source 6].

### Tools and safety
Required tools include **panel cutout tools**, a **large slotted or Phillips screwdriver**, and a **torque wrench** for tightening the mounting clips [Source 6].

Before making the panel cutout:
- **Disconnect all electrical power from the panel** [Source 6].
- Make sure the area around the cutout is clear and the panel is clean of debris, oil, or other chemicals [Source 6].
- Ensure metal cuttings do not enter installed components and that cutout edges have no burrs or sharp edges [Source 6].
- Failure to follow these warnings can result in personal injury or damage to panel components [Source 6].

### Panel mounting steps
1. **Cut an opening** in the panel using the panel cutout template shipped with the terminal or the cutout dimensions in publication **2715P-UM001** [Source 2].  
2. **Place the terminal screen-down** on a clean, flat surface and avoid scratching or damaging the screen [Source 2].  
3. **Position the gasket on the bezel**, with the gasket alignment plugs facing the bezel alignment features; the gasket forms a compression seal, and sealing compounds must not be used [Source 2].  
4. **Slip the inside corners of the gasket under the corners of the bezel shroud** [Source 2].  
5. **Press each gasket alignment plug into the bezel alignment feature**; the plug snaps into place when fully seated [Source 2].  
6. **Place the terminal in the panel cutout** and hold it so it does not fall out [Source 6].  
7. **Position the backing plate over the terminal**, making sure the flat side of the backing plate faces away from the panel [Source 2, 6].  
8. **Slide the ends of the mounting clips into the slots on the terminal** [Source 2].  
9. **Tighten the mounting clip screws by hand** until the backing plate contacts the panel uniformly [Source 2].  
10. **Torque the mounting clip screws to 2.3…2.6 N•m (20…23 lb•in)** using the specified sequence [Source 2].  
11. The clips loosen as the adjacent clip is tightened, so **repeat the torque step until all mounting clips are at the specified torque** [Source 2].

For complete installation instructions, see publication **2715P-UM001** [Source 6]. For stainless-steel terminal installation information, see publication **2715P-PC002** [Source 1].
per_question.expected_answer: 1) Cut the panel opening using the shipped cutout template (or the user-manual dimensions). 2) Place the terminal screen-down on a clean, flat surface. 3) Position the gasket on the bezel with the alignment plugs facing the bezel alignment features and 4) press each plug into place (compression seal, no sealing compounds). 5) Place the terminal in the cutout. 6) Position the backing plate over the terminal. 7) Slide the mounting clips into the slots. 8) Hand-tighten the clip screws until the backing plate contacts the panel uniformly. 9) Torque the clip screws to 2.3…2.6 N•m (20…23 lb•in) in the specified sequence, 10) repeating until all clips are at torque.

per_question.question: How is the mounting arm tube fitted to the mounting arm adapter of a Beckhoff CP39xx control panel, and what torques are specified?
per_question.answer:
For the Beckhoff CP39xx control panel, the specified torques are:

- **Mounting arm tube on the mounting arm adapter**
  - Retighten the hexagon socket screw with **3 Nm** [Source 2].
  - Tighten the slotted nut of the mounting arm adapter clockwise with a hook wrench size 58–62 using **20 Nm** [Source 2].

- **Installing the mounting arm adapter to the adapter plate**
  - Tighten the four M6 screws with **6 Nm** [Source 7].

Insert the tube 50.2 mm into the adapter up to the stop. 4. Retighten the hexagon socket screw to 3 Nm. 5. Tighten the adapter's slotted nut clockwise with a size 58-62 hook wrench (C9900-Z263) to 20 Nm. (Adapters fit Rittal/Rolec 48 mm tubes.)

per_question.question: Using the SIMATIC IPC Panel Drivers and Tools (PDT) UPDD Console, how do you perform the extended 25-point touch calibration on a SIMATIC IFP V2 with resistive single-touch screen?
per_question.answer:
For a resistive single-touch screen on SIMATIC IPC/IFP, the UPDD Console in PDT V1.7 supports an extended/advanced calibration with up to 25 calibration points; this is recommended when special accuracy requirements exist, and the calibration data are stored in the operating system on the PC [Source 1]. The touch screen is pre-calibrated with a 3-point calibration in the delivery state, and the 25-point calibration can be used if the 3-point calibration accuracy is not sufficient [Source 1][Source 3].

Procedure for extended 25-point touch calibration:

1. Open the UPDD Console dialog; the manual indicates opening the Configuration Center and going to the “UPDD Settings” tab [Source 3][Source 8].  
2. Select the touch controller of the device you want to calibrate in the header of the dialog [Source 3].  
3. Click the “Calibration” tab [Source 3].  
4. Deactivate the option “Use eeprom storage” [Source 3].  
5. Enter the value “25” under “Number of points” [Source 3].  
6. Click the “Calibrate” button; the calibration screen is displayed in the selected display [Source 3].  
7. Touch the corresponding selections one after the other; each entry is confirmed by a check mark, and the next selection is displayed [Source 3].  
8. Confirm all input prompts, such as arrows or crosses in the center, until the complete screen has been calibrated [Source 3].  
9. Finally, press “Confirm” for the input prompt [Source 3].  

If the screen does not respond to touch as expected, check the controller selected in the UPDD Console and repeat the calibration; only an active touch controller can be calibrated, and a removed touch controller is displayed in red [Source 3][Source 6]. If several touch devices are connected, all touch devices must be calibrated with an extended calibration of at least 9 points [Source 2].
per_question.expected_answer: 1. Open the "UPDD Console" dialog. 2. Select the touch controller of the device in the dialog header. 3. Click the "Calibration" tab. 4. Deactivate "Use eeprom storage". 5. Enter "25" under "Number of points". 6. Click "Calibrate" (calibration screen appears on the selected display). 7. Touch the selections one after the other (each confirmed with a check mark). 8. Confirm all prompts until the whole screen is calibrated. 9. Press "Confirm" at the final prompt. Unlike the 3-point calibration, the data is stored in the OS on the PC, not in the device EEPROM.
per_question.rewritten_query: SIMATIC IPC Panel Drivers and Tools UPDD Console extended 25-point touch calibration SIMATIC IFP V2 resistive single-touch screen

per_question.question: What is the procedure for installing the BootOS or system application on a Mitsubishi GOT2000 (GT27/GT25) from an SD card using the utility?
per_question.answer:
For GOT2000 GT27/GT25, the utility manual states that “for the installation using GOT, the data storage that is storing BootOS or the system application is required” [Source 2]. The listed methods are:

- “[To Memory Card] from GT Designer3”  
- “Uploading from another GOT (the package data has been installed)”  
- “Using an SD card that stores data with OS boot drive set to A drive” [Source 1, 2, 4]

## 1. Prepare the SD card

When installing BootOS/system application/package data into an SD card, “be sure to execute by the utility of another GOT or GT Designer3” [Source 1, 2, 4]. The installation “is not executed properly with the SD card to which data is uploaded from the utility of GOT or copied by software other than GT Designer3” [Source 1, 2]. Also, “note the available capacity of the SD card,” which can be confirmed by “[To Memory Card]” or “[Write Option]” of GT Designer3 [Source 1, 2]; another section also refers to “[Write to Memory Card]” or “[Write Option]” [Source 4].

BootOS is “installed at factory shipment,” while the basic system application “is not installed in the GOT at factory shipment” [Source 3]. To execute the GOT utility, install BootOS and system applications on the “C drive (built-in flash memory)” or “set the boot drive of the package data to [A:SD card] and insert an SD card with the package data” [Source 3].

## 2. Install by starting the GOT with the SD card

The startup method transfers “all the system applications and project data stored in the data storage … when powering on the GOT,” and is effective when “the GOT utility cannot be displayed” or “the system application is not installed” [Source 6].

Procedure:

1. “Power OFF the GOT, and install the SD card where the BootOS, system application or project data is stored in the SD card interface of the GOT” [Source 5, 7].  
2. “Close the cover of the SD card interface of the GOT” [Source 5].  
3. “Power on the GOT. While touching the lower right side of the GOT screen, power on the GOT. (1-point press installation function)” [Source 7, 8].  
   - Another procedure section also says to “hold down the S.MODE switch and power on the GOT”; for GT2505-V, “power on the GOT while touching the lower right of the screen” [Source 5].  
   - However, “when the data storage that stores data with the OS boot drive set to the A drive is used, the S.MODE switch-pressing installation function is not available” [Source 5].  
4. During installation, “the BootOS or system application is installed in the built-in flash memory” [Source 5, 7]. “Do not pull out the SD card or power OFF the GOT while the SD card access LED is lit” [Source 5, 7].  
5. “The GOT restarts automatically after the installation is completed” [Source 5, 7]. If the system application is already installed, “touch the [OK] button to restart the GOT” [Source 5].  
6. “After confirming normal restart, confirm that the SD card access LED is not lit, and remove the SD card from the SD card interface of the GOT” [Source 5, 7].

## 3. Install using the utility / data-copy function

The utility method works by “operating the utility, select[ing] the system application or project data stored in the data storage and transfer[ing] them to the GOT” [Source 6].

Procedure:

1. “Power OFF the GOT, and attach the SD card which stores the basic system application and communication driver to the GOT” [Source 7, 8].  
2. “While touching the upper left corner of the GOT screen, power ON the GOT” [Source 7, 8].  
3. “When the screen shown on the left appears, select the [Data copy]” [Source 7, 8].

## 4. Important installation precautions

- If installing both BootOS and system applications, “after completing BootOS installation, install system applications” [Source 6].  
- “When installing BootOS, the built-in flash memory in the GOT is initialized and goes to the status at factory shipment. (All system applications and project data are erased.)” [Source 6].  
- “Installation cannot be interrupted.” Do not perform “powering off the GOT,” “pressing the reset button of the GOT,” or “removing the data storage” during installation [Source 6].
per_question.expected_answer: 1. Insert the SD card holding the BootOS/system application/project data into the GOT's SD card interface. 2. Close the SD card interface cover. 3. Open the data control function screen in the utility and install the BootOS/system application from the SD card. 4. The SD card access LED stays lit during installation - do not remove the card or open the cover. 5. The GOT restarts automatically when installation completes. 6. After a normal restart, confirm the access LED is off and remove the SD card.
per_question.rewritten_query: Mitsubishi GOT2000 GT27 GT25 BootOS system application installation procedure SD card utility

per_question.question: How do I enter Calibrate Mode and calibrate the touch panel on an Omron NB-series HMI using the rear DIP switches?
per_question.answer:
To enter **Calibrate Mode** using the rear DIP switches:

1. On the back side of the NB Unit, set **DIP switch SW1 to OFF** and **SW2 to ON** [Source 1, 7].  
2. Restart the unit by pressing the **Reset switch** [Source 1]; the manual also describes powering the unit on with these settings, indicated by the **POWER LED turning green** [Source 7].  
3. When you touch the panel, a **“+”** appears; track and touch the **“+”** until it disappears and **“TP Adjust Success!”** is displayed [Source 1, 7].  
4. Set both **SW1 and SW2 to OFF**, then press the **Reset switch** again [Source 1].
per_question.expected_answer: 1. Set rear DIP switches SW1 to OFF and SW2 to ON. 2. Press the Reset switch to restart the NB unit into Calibrate Mode. 3. Touch each '+' shown on the screen (a touch sound confirms each) until the '+' disappears and 'TP Adjust Success!' is displayed. 4. Set both SW1 and SW2 to OFF. 5. Press the Reset switch again. (Alternatively, a Function Key component set to 'Touch Calibration' starts calibration from a project screen.)

per_question.question: How is a Pro-face SP5000 box module (e.g. SP-5B40) attached to the display module or DC power supply adapter?
per_question.answer:
The SP-5B40 is the SP5000 Series **Open Box**, model number **PFXSP5B40** [Source 1, 7]. It can be attached to a compatible **Display Module** or to the **DC Power Supply Adapter for Box Module** (Pro-face model **PFXZCDADEXP1**) [Source 1, 4].

**Installation/attachment steps**
- Before installing or removing accessories, hardware, or cables:  
  - Remove all power from the device.  
  - Unplug the power cable from both the Display Module or DC Power Supply Adapter for Box Module and the power supply.  
  - Use a properly rated voltage sensing device to confirm power is off.  
  - Replace and secure all covers/elements before applying power. [Source 4, 6]
- If mounting the product vertically, install the Box Module onto the Display Module or DC Power Supply Adapter for Box Module **before** attaching the unit to the panel. [Source 4]
- Place the Display Module or DC Power Supply Adapter for Box Module on a clean, level surface with the screen facing downward. [Source 4]
- Pull the **LOCK** forward on the top of the Box Module to release the lock. [Source 4]
- Fully push the **LOCK** on the top of the Box Module to mount the Box Module on the Display Module or DC Power Supply Adapter for Box Module. [Source 8]

**Compatibility/electrical notes**
- SP-5B40 supports only Display Modules with a resolution of **XGA or less**. [Source 1]
- The hardware manual also states that SP-5B40 supports any listed Display Module except **SP-5700WC, SP-5800WC, and SP-5600TA**. [Source 7]
- The Box Module’s rated input voltage is **12 Vdc**, supplied from the Display Module or DC Power Supply Adapter. [Source 2]
per_question.expected_answer: 1) Pull the LOCK on the top of the Box Module forward to release the lock. 2) Insert the protruding points on the bottom left and right of the Box Module into the two holes on the back of the Display Module (or DC Power Supply Adapter for Box Module) to attach it. 3) Fully push the LOCK on the top of the Box Module to secure it to the Display Module or adapter.

per_question.question: What is the installation process for mounting a Beijer X2 pro 4 B2 HMI panel in a cabinet door?
per_question.answer:
For the **Beijer X2 Pro 4 B2**, the provided sources support the following cabinet-door installation/mounting process:

1. **Preparation**
   - A **Phillips/slot screwdriver** is needed [Source 8].
   - **Unpack and check the delivery**; if damage is found, notify the supplier [Source 8].
   - Place the panel on a stable surface during installation, because dropping it may cause damage [Source 8].

2. **Cutout / space requirements**
   - Cut the correct opening using the **cut-out dimensions in the outline drawing** [Source 8].
   - A separate cut-out drawing is available for download from the Beijer Electronics web site [Source 8].
   - For the X2 Pro 4 B2, the **maximum installation plate thickness is 11 mm** [Source 8].
   - The space-requirements drawing shows dimensions: **100 mm, 104 mm, 50 mm, 50 mm, 100 mm, 100 mm, 43 mm, and 145 mm** [Source 8].

3. **Mechanical fastening**
   - The provided X2 Pro 4 B2 excerpt stops after the cutout step [Source 8].
   - The related **X2 Pro 15 B2** installation section says to make sure the mounting surface of the cutout is **smooth and cleaned from burrs or debris**, install the HMI panel into the cutout, and secure it by screwing the **slotted thumb screw clockwise** so the built-in bracket flips out and tightens against the cabinet [Source 2].
   - Tighten the screws to **0.7 ± 0.2 Nm** [Source 2].
   - If a front panel seal is critical, use a torque wrench to ensure all screws are torqued within that specification [Source 2].

4. **Cabinet-door grounding for the X2 Pro 4 B2**
   - The mounting clamps **do not provide a secure grounding connection** between the panel and the device cabinet [Source 6].
   - Connect a correctly sized wire between the **quickconnect terminal connector on the HMI panel** and the **panel chassis** [Source 6].
   - Connect a correctly sized wire or grounding braid between the **panel chassis** and the **closest grounding point on the door** [Source 6].
   - Connect a **strong but short grounding braid** between the **door** and the **device cabinet** [Source 6].
   - Twist the cables onto the **24 V DC feed**; 2 turns around the ferrite core provide 4 times the suppression of 1 turn, and 3 turns provide 9 times [Source 6].

5. **Cable connection**
   - The related X2 Pro 15 B2 manual says to connect the cables in the specified order **A, B, C, D** [Source 2].
   - Cable B uses **14–20 AWG** with **180–220 N-cm torque** [Source 2].
   - Cable D has a recommended cross-section of **1.5 mm²** [Source 2].
per_question.expected_answer: 1) Unpack and check the delivery; notify the supplier of any damage. 2) Cut the opening using the cut-out dimensions in the outline drawing (130 x 89 mm). 3) Make sure the mounting surface of the cutout is smooth and free of burrs/debris. 4) Install the HMI panel into the cutout. 5) Secure it using all fastening holes and the provided brackets and screws, tightened to 0.5 - 1.0 Nm. 6) Where the front seal (IP54+/NEMA-4X) is critical, use a torque wrench to confirm the screw torque. 7) Connect the cables in the specified order (A, then B power using 14-20 AWG at 180-220 N-cm, then C Ethernet, then D). 8) Carefully remove the protective film from the display, avoiding static.
